A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Graph-S3. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching material across the changed formatting and appendix organization.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figure 3 report original QA experiments, ablations and retrieval-size results on WebQSP, CWQ and MetaQA.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds success and failure case studies in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The synthesis, refinement, SFT-to-GRPO training, rewards and three-action retriever are retained. However, Equation 1 changes Explore's domain from G to the perception window G^p, while the prose and prompt still describe full-graph expansion. Whether this represents an intended procedural change or an equation error is unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WebQSP, CWQ and MetaQA with its one-, two- and three-hop tasks. The added movie-domain cases illustrate retained QA coverage without establishing a new dataset, domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the no-graph and no-retriever controls, one-/two-/three-hop RAG, ToG, LightRAG, G-Retriever and KG-Agent. Appendix C's additional examples reuse RAG and G-Retriever rather than introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, model configurations and training budgets remain unchanged, including 9,035 SFT instances, 3,504 RL instances and three SFT plus fifteen RL epochs. The added qualitative cases do not document a revised quantitative evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a successful high-degree-entity retrieval case and a co-writer-query failure, with trajectories and discussion of baseline errors. The existing component ablations, reward-supervision comparison and retrieval-size analysis remain, while v1's original reasoning example moves to Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and retrieval-count plots without repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2 introduces no new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The numerical scores in Tables 1–3 are unchanged, and Figure 3 retains the retrieval-count findings. Appendix C adds reported outcomes: correct release years for the Sarah Polley query, RAG and G-Retriever errors, and Graph-S3 returning film titles instead of Jane Anderson's co-writers.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes the formal exploration definition from neighboring triples in G to triples already in G^p, creating an inconsistency with the stated expansion operation. The other mathematical edits largely rename notation or replace the transition equation with equivalent prose; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain synthetic stepwise supervision, two-stage training and compact interactive graph retrieval. The abstract retains the claimed average gains of 8.1% accuracy and 9.7% F1, and the introduction retains the state-of-the-art and retrieval-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of high-degree noise pruning and a co-writer failure attributed to self-verification bias and attention to named entities. Section 4.2 also expands precision-related and cross-backbone interpretations. These extend v1's more general explanations and successful illustrative trace.

D1.justification: Model names, training counts, hyperparameters, hardware, timing and Table 4 are retained, with implementation information consolidated in Appendix A. The interactive prompt is reformatted with equivalent instructions, and both versions only promise a future code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including RACQC, SE-Search, VideoSeg-R1, ARK and Unlocking Implicit Experience, while removing LLAGA, GraphGPT and Edge et al.'s graph-RAG paper. The central positioning against one-shot retrieval and sparse outcome supervision remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, and Section 4.2 becomes a sequence of named interpretive observations. The appendices are reorganized into A–D, a limitations section is added, author information is revised, and v1's writing-assistance disclosure is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting. Figure 3 is redrawn from a horizontal arrangement into a 2-by-2 arrangement, tables are resized and relocated, ablation labels and emphasis change, and the prompt and new case studies receive revised boxed displays.

improvement.justification: Appendix C provides a limited gain in transparency by showing both successful pruning and a concrete failure involving premature termination and the wrong answer type. The reorganized discussion helps readers interpret retained results. These benefits are tempered by the new Equation 1 inconsistency and an attention-bias explanation unsupported by attention measurements; quantitative validation remains unchanged.
